A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SwissGov-RSD study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–J. Relocated material and identifiable redactions in the annotation instructions do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, human-annotation agreement, label-projection validation, and inference-time measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, annotation analyses, label-projection validation, and timing measurements.

M1.justification: DiffAlign, few-shot labeling, supervised fine-tuning, encoder token regression, and GPT-4o-mini label projection retain their procedures and objectives. Moving label projection from Section 4.4 into Section 5.3 and correcting illustrative labels do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 224 SwissGov document groups covering EN–DE, EN–FR, and EN–IT, alongside the same iSTS-RSD/PAWS training and evaluation coverage. The Italian extension and seven-language-pair synthetic evaluation were already present in v2.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the corresponding evaluations are retained. Table 12 changes ModernBERT-base to ModernBERT-large, matching v2’s setup and Tables 3, 10, and 11; the unchanged scores support treating this as a naming correction rather than a new comparator.

E3.justification: Reported model configurations receive limited corrections: Table 10 changes gte-multilingual-base from 685B to 300M parameters, Table 12 identifies ModernBERT-large, and Table 15 changes Llama-3.2 to Llama-3.1. These documentation revisions do not establish reruns. Splits, training budgets, evaluation sample counts, and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: The prediction examples, token-position analysis, annotator-discrepancy analysis, label-projection checks, Kendall comparison, and timing analysis are retained. Appendix F is relocated, and Section 5.4 summarizes the existing Kendall findings; neither adds an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seeds, repeated training runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Annotation sampling, agreement reporting, and the timing averages over 100 encoder inferences and 10 LLM inferences remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The corresponding benchmark correlations, annotation statistics, projection-edit rates, output-failure rates, timing measurements, and plotted findings are unchanged. Corrections to model descriptions and illustrative prompt or diagram labels do not introduce new empirical outcomes.

T1.justification: Section 3 refines the definition of spans used for agreement calculations: v2 describes token spans with a positive label, while v3 explicitly specifies tokens sharing the same contiguous positive label. The IoU and DiffAlign equations remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The dataset novelty, benchmark contribution, and substantial synthetic-to-naturalistic performance gap remain the core claims. The introduction reorganizes these into three bullets and specifies existing model counts; it does not introduce a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: The limitations discussion newly emphasizes that the English-centric, closely related language setting should be comparatively favorable, yet models already struggle there. The discussion also makes the proposed focus on preserving structured sequence-labeling output more explicit. Existing explanations about generalization, segmentation, and annotation disagreement remain.

D1.justification: v3 corrects model metadata and adds a missing label in Appendix D’s second projection example. Appendix A.2 redacts the annotation-tool repository address and example server URLs, reducing setup detail. The main public code and dataset links, hyperparameters, hardware information, and annotation guidelines remain available.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Publication details are updated for Kreutzer et al. (2020) and Wastl et al. (2025), and attribution is clarified without adding a new line of related work.

P1.justification: v3 makes numerous local grammar, terminology, and tense corrections, restructures the contribution list, moves label projection into the training-data section, and removes the redundant Appendix D.1 heading. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The architecture and label-distribution figures exchange numbering and move closer to their discussions; several tables and Appendix F are relocated. Captions and cross-references are clarified, and the architecture diagram fixes JSON formatting and punctuation labels. The figure and table inventory is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves technical accuracy and readability through corrected model descriptions, the repaired Appendix D example, clearer figure annotations, and better organization. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. Redacting annotation-tool URLs modestly reduces setup detail, but the primary code and dataset access information is retained; the net improvement is limited.
